title: Chaos Chess! Because every chess game should have dragons attack mid-match.
author: JordanMilas
selftext:
Several years ago I had launched a website [chaoschess.online](http://chaoschess.online) where players could play a chess variant that used SVG images for traditional pieces and would have "crazy events" occur mid-way through a match. After using Coursera's study program on Blender and a metric ton of pdf guidebooks, I rebuilt the game into a 3D environment.  I used Google's Gemini for the art asset cards for each event, and Opus 5.5 helped me with setting up the story-campaign videos in Google Flow. Oh an obviously a metric ton of debugging help was performed by codex and claude code so the game could reach its final state.

Here's the basic gist:

* There's a 10-chapter story campaign about old chess pieces (eg, Empress, camel, lion, etc) coming back with a vengeance
* Each match features a Chaos Event (a flood, volcano, witch's curse, blizzard) that impacts both players
* Also there's potential for a pawn uprising, where all the pawns on the board revolt, crown a new red king, and attack both white and black pieces as a third player
* The game also features 7 scenarios, that test your skill against varying difficulties. A viking invasion keeps pumping 3rd-player berserkers each turn onto the board, and your only goal is to outlast the opponent king. A dragons vs vampires scenario includes a day/night cycle in chess that modifies the pieces abilities. And a zombie attack is chess meets minesweeper.
* To overcome the bad stuff happening, you get to add two Champion pieces to your board to fight on your behalf. These pieces have special abilities and moves. The Executioner can leap over pieces in front of it and eliminate the first opponent piece in its path. The lion piece can move twice, just like its historical piece. The Thief moves like a pawn but can attack diagonally backwards in addition to forwards. The Necromancer can return a captured piece back to your ranks. And so on....
* Several gorgeous environments and the board view can be adjusted so you have full view of the action
